```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2024_borofalan"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2024_borofalan"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/ph17030301>

L-4-[10B]boronophenylalanine (BPA; INN borofalan (10B)) is the boron carrier
used in boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT). The radiation dose delivered
during neutron irradiation depends on the boron-10 concentration in blood and
tissue at the time of irradiation, and blood cannot be sampled while the
patient is in the irradiation room. Kim et al. built a population PK model of
whole-blood boron-10 after an intravenous BPA infusion and used it as the
prior for Bayesian (MAP) prediction of the mean blood boron level during the
irradiation window.

# Population

The model was fitted to 377 whole-blood boron-10 concentrations from 27 cancer
patients given an intravenous infusion of 10B-enriched BPA (as the
BPA-fructose complex). No new clinical data were collected: the
concentration-time points were digitised by the authors from seven published
clinical reports (Kim 2024 references 8 and 10-15), which cover glioma /
glioblastoma, malignant melanoma and head and neck cancer patients treated in
Finland, the USA, China, an EORTC trial and Japan. Doses and infusion durations
differ between the source reports (Figure 2 shows 250 mg/kg over 65 min and
290 mg/kg over 120 min); the paper's own simulations use 500 mg/kg over
180 min. No demographics or covariates were available to the authors, and the
final model has none (Kim 2024 Methods 2.1).

The same information is available programmatically via
`rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2024_borofalan"))$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each
`ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Kim_2024_borofalan.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lkel` (K10) | log(0.006) 1/min | Table 2 |
| `lk12` (K12) | log(0.023) 1/min | Table 2 |
| `lk21` (K21) | log(0.012) 1/min | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (V1) | log(0.252) L/kg | Table 2 (printed "L"; per-kg per Figure 4A, see below) |
| `etalkel` | 0.050 (CV 22.6%) | Table 2, IIV K10 |
| `etalk12` | 0.071 (CV 27.2%) | Table 2, IIV K12 |
| `etalk21` | 0.037 (CV 19.4%) | Table 2, IIV K21 |
| `etalvc` | 0.061 (CV 25.0%) | Table 2, IIV V1 |
| `addSd` | sqrt(0.540) ug/g | Table 2, eps1 (additive) |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.001) | Table 2, eps2 (proportional) |
| Individual parameters `P_i = P_TV * exp(eta)` | n/a | Methods 2.1 |
| Two-compartment linear disposition | n/a | Results 3.1 |
| Boron-10 / BPA factor `10/208.21` | n/a | Methods 2.1 |
| `Cobs = Cpred + eps1 + eps2 * Cpred` | n/a | Results 3.1 |

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Kim_2024_borofalan")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
```

# Unit check against Figure 4A (deterministic)

Figure 4A of the paper shows the platform's Bayesian fit for a simulated
patient given 500 mg/kg BPA over 180 min, and prints that patient's
individual parameters (`K1 = 0.021817 1/min`, `K2 = 0.01085 1/min`,
`K3 = 0.0059167 1/min`, `V1 = 0.22902 l/kg`) together with the nine blood
boron-10 values the fit was conditioned on. Solving the packaged model with
those individual parameters must reproduce the printed values. This pins the
per-kilogram volume, the mg/kg dosing unit and the 10/208.21 boron-10
conversion together: getting any one of them wrong moves the curve by a
factor of 70 (body weight) or 21 (the conversion), not by a few percent.

```{r fig4a-gate}
fig4a <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~published,
  60, 18.999,
  120, 27.999,
  180, 34.999,
  190, 31.999,
  200, 27.999,
  210, 25.999,
  220, 24.999,
  230, 22.999,
  240, 21.999
)

ev_fig4a <- rxode2::et(amt = 500, rate = 500 / 180, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 480, by = 2))

sim_fig4a <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typical,
  events = ev_fig4a,
  params = c(
    lk12 = log(0.021817),
    lk21 = log(0.01085),
    lkel = log(0.0059167),
    lvc = log(0.22902)
  )
) |>
  as.data.frame()

chk_fig4a <- fig4a |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(sim_fig4a, time, Cc), by = "time") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Cc - published) / published)

knitr::kable(
  chk_fig4a |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Time (min)" = time,
      "Figure 4A (ug/g)" = published,
      "Packaged model (ug/g)" = Cc,
      "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
    ),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Blood boron-10 at the Figure 4A sampling times, solved with the printed individual parameters."
)

# The Figure 4A values are the patient's sampled (simulated-observed) levels,
# so they carry residual error around the fitted curve; the realised
# differences are within -3.0% to +1.5%. A unit or conversion error would
# shift every row by more than an order of magnitude.
stopifnot(
  nrow(chk_fig4a) == 9L,
  !anyNA(chk_fig4a$Cc),
  abs(median(chk_fig4a$pct_diff)) < 2,
  max(abs(chk_fig4a$pct_diff)) < 5
)
```

```{r fig4a-plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(sim_fig4a, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig4a, aes(time, published), colour = "red") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)",
    y = "Blood boron-10 (ug/g)",
    title = "Figure 4A -- 500 mg/kg BPA over 180 min",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4A of Kim 2024 (individual Bayesian parameters printed in the figure)."
  )
```

# Replicate Figure 2: individual visual predictive checks

Figure 2 of the paper shows the model's median and 95% prediction interval for
two of the source patients: patient 2101 (250 mg/kg over 65 min) and
patient 3101 (290 mg/kg over 120 min). The block below simulates 200 virtual
patients per regimen with between-subject variability and residual error.

```{r fig2-cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240301)

regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~dose, ~dur, ~tend,
  "ID 2101: 250 mg/kg over 65 min", 250, 65, 1200,
  "ID 3101: 290 mg/kg over 120 min", 290, 120, 300
)
n_per_arm <- 200L

make_regimen <- function(i, n = n_per_arm) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  ids <- (i - 1L) * n + seq_len(n)
  obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, r$tend, by = 5), r$dur)))
  dose_rows <- tibble::tibble(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = r$dose, rate = r$dose / r$dur,
    evid = 1L, cmt = "central"
  )
  obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = r$regimen) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

events_fig2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), make_regimen))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_fig2[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_fig2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_fig2, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r fig2-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
vpc_fig2 <- sim_fig2 |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    lo = quantile(sim, 0.025),
    med = median(sim),
    hi = quantile(sim, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc_fig2, aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "salmon", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(colour = "darkred") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)",
    y = "Blood boron-10 (ppm)",
    title = "Figure 2 -- median and 95% prediction interval",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Kim 2024."
  )
```

The published medians peak at about 24 ppm at the end of the 65-min infusion
(patient 2101) and about 22 ppm at the end of the 120-min infusion
(patient 3101); the published 95% interval at the 2101 peak spans roughly
14-41 ppm. The typical-value solve below checks the peaks deterministically.

```{r fig2-gate}
ev_typ_fig2 <- events_fig2 |>
  dplyr::filter(id %in% c(1L, n_per_arm + 1L))
typ_fig2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = ev_typ_fig2, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame()

peak_fig2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~time, ~figure2_median,
  "ID 2101: 250 mg/kg over 65 min", 65, 24.4,
  "ID 3101: 290 mg/kg over 120 min", 120, 22.0
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::select(typ_fig2, regimen, time, Cc),
    by = c("regimen", "time")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Cc - figure2_median) / figure2_median)

knitr::kable(
  peak_fig2 |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Regimen" = regimen,
      "End of infusion (min)" = time,
      "Figure 2 median, digitised (ppm)" = figure2_median,
      "Packaged typical value (ppm)" = Cc,
      "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
    ),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "End-of-infusion typical-value concentration vs. the Figure 2 median."
)

# Deterministic typical-value solve against a digitised median (about
# +/-0.5 ppm reading precision); realised differences are +1.6% and -0.1%.
stopifnot(!anyNA(peak_fig2$Cc), all(abs(peak_fig2$pct_diff) < 8))
```

# Irradiation-window simulation (500 mg/kg over 180 min)

The paper's sampling-schedule simulations use 500 mg/kg infused over 180 min,
with neutron irradiation from 240 to 300 min. Section 3.3 states that the 95%
interval of the mean blood boron level during irradiation was taken to be
10-30 ppm based on the population model.

```{r sim-500}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240302)
n_sub <- 200L
obs_500 <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 300, by = 5), seq(310, 2880, by = 30))))
events_500 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(
    id = seq_len(n_sub), time = 0, amt = 500, rate = 500 / 180,
    evid = 1L, cmt = "central"
  ),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_sub), time = obs_500) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "500 mg/kg over 180 min") |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_500 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_500, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()

# Mean concentration over the 240-300 min irradiation window, per subject
# (trapezoidal over the 5-min grid), using the individual prediction.
window_mean <- sim_500 |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 240, time <= 300) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cavg = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2) / 60,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

q_window <- quantile(window_mean$cavg, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Statistic = c("2.5th percentile", "Median", "97.5th percentile"),
    "Mean blood boron-10, 240-300 min (ppm)" = unname(q_window)
  ),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Simulated distribution of the irradiation-window mean (paper: 10-30 ppm)."
)

# Centre and robust envelope only. On a 5000-subject cohort the model gives
# a median of 18.7 ppm (typical value 19.1), 10th percentile 12.6 and 90th
# percentile 27.5; each bound below is at least 4 standard errors of a
# 200-subject quantile away. The 2.5/97.5% tails are reported, not gated.
stopifnot(
  q_window[["50%"]] > 15, q_window[["50%"]] < 25,
  quantile(window_mean$cavg, 0.1) > 10,
  quantile(window_mean$cavg, 0.9) < 31
)
```

The simulated 95% interval of the irradiation-window mean (about 10-33 ppm)
agrees with the 10-30 ppm interval the paper states for its population model.

```{r sim-500-plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
sim_500 |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 720) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    lo = quantile(Cc, 0.025), med = median(Cc), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 240, xmax = 300, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)",
    y = "Blood boron-10 (ug/g)",
    title = "500 mg/kg BPA over 180 min (shaded: irradiation window)",
    caption = "Individual predictions; median and 95% interval of 200 virtual patients."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA, so PKNCA is used to summarise the simulated
500 mg/kg cohort and, on a typical-value solve, to check AUC and terminal
half-life against the closed-form two-compartment values
(`AUCinf = F * Dose / (kel * V1)` with `F = 10/208.21` the boron-10 fraction,
and `t1/2 = log(2) / beta`).

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_500 |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
nca_conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_conc,
  nca_conc |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, treatment, time)

nca_dose <- events_500 |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = intervals
))
knitr::kable(
  summary(nca_res),
  caption = "PKNCA summary, 500 mg/kg BPA over 180 min (Cc in ug/g, time in min)."
)
```

```{r pknca-typical}
typ_500 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typical,
  events = dplyr::filter(events_500, id == 1L),
  keep = "treatment"
) |>
  as.data.frame()
if (is.null(typ_500$id)) typ_500$id <- 1L

nca_typ <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
    dplyr::select(typ_500, id, time, Cc, treatment),
    Cc ~ time | treatment + id
  ),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
    dplyr::filter(nca_dose, id == 1L),
    amt ~ time | treatment + id
  ),
  intervals = intervals
)) |>
  as.data.frame()

th <- exp(ui$theta)
kel <- th[["lkel"]]
k12 <- th[["lk12"]]
k21 <- th[["lk21"]]
v1 <- th[["lvc"]]
ksum <- kel + k12 + k21
beta <- (ksum - sqrt(ksum^2 - 4 * kel * k21)) / 2
closed <- c(
  aucinf.obs = 500 * (10 / 208.21) / (kel * v1),
  half.life = log(2) / beta
)

cmp_typ <- tibble::tibble(
  parameter = names(closed),
  closed_form = unname(closed),
  pknca = vapply(
    names(closed),
    function(p) nca_typ$PPORRES[nca_typ$PPTESTCD == p],
    numeric(1)
  )
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (pknca - closed_form) / closed_form)

knitr::kable(
  cmp_typ |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "NCA parameter" = parameter,
      "Closed form" = closed_form,
      "PKNCA (typical value)" = pknca,
      "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
    ),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Typical-value PKNCA vs. closed-form AUCinf (ug*min/g) and terminal half-life (min)."
)

# Deterministic solve; the residual difference is trapezoidal error on the
# 30-min tail grid and the extrapolation from the last point.
stopifnot(all(abs(cmp_typ$pct_diff) < 3))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **V1 is per kilogram.** Table 2 prints the unit of V1 as "L", but the dose is
  given in mg/kg and Figure 4A prints an individual V1 of "0.22902 l/kg". Only
  a per-kilogram volume reproduces the 20-35 ppm blood levels of Figures 2
  and 4A (the deterministic Figure 4A check above), so the model is coded per
  kilogram: dose in mg/kg of BPA, V1 in L/kg.
- **Boron-10 conversion and units.** The model state holds BPA (mg/kg); the
  output is boron-10, `Cc = central * (10/208.21) / vc`, using the paper's
  factor (Methods 2.1). mg/L is reported as ug/g (ppm), which assumes a blood
  density of 1 g/mL, as the paper does.
- **Residual-error scale.** Table 2 prints the additive and proportional
  residual terms (0.540 and 0.001) without saying whether they are variances
  or standard deviations. The maintainers read them as NONMEM `$SIGMA`
  variances, the same raw-estimate scale as the IIV rows of the same table
  (whose CV% values are exactly `sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`), so
  `addSd = sqrt(0.540) = 0.73 ug/g` and `propSd = sqrt(0.001) = 3.2%`. Under
  the alternative SD reading (0.54 ug/g and 0.1%) the 95% prediction interval
  of Figure 2 moves visibly only in the low-concentration tail (by about
  0.3 ppm at 1200 min for patient 2101), because the between-subject
  variability dominates; the figure cannot distinguish the two readings.
- **No covariates and no covariance.** The source data were digitised from
  published figures, so no patient characteristics were available; Table 2
  reports a diagonal IIV matrix.
- **Figure 2 medians digitised.** The end-of-infusion medians used in the
  Figure 2 check (24.4 and 22.0 ppm) were read from Figure 2 by the
  maintainers (about +/-0.5 ppm reading precision).
- **No published NCA.** The paper reports no NCA parameters, so there is no
  simulated-vs-published NCA table; PKNCA is checked against closed-form
  values instead.
- Europe PMC links no erratum or correction notice to this article as of
  2026-10-29.
